title: Import Once
statement: Implement `solve(calls)`. `calls` is a list of module names looked up in order. A name is loaded only the first time it appears. Return a dict with `loads`, the list of names that actually loaded, and `cache`, a dict mapping each loaded name to the string `mod:` plus that name. Later lookups must not append another load.
constraints: cache keys are the module names
hints: Keep a dict from name to the built module string.
Append to loads only when the name is missing from that dict.
The module string is the prefix mod: plus the name. Do not number the loads.
editorial: sys.modules is a cache keyed by module name. The first import calls the loader and stores the module. A second import returns the stored object and does not run the module body again. This function is that cache, with a visible list of the loads that really happened.
